summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with HIV and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for shortness of breath and hypotension following an extra dialysis session. She developed symptomatic hypotension with a blood pressure of 82/40, likely due to excessive fluid removal, and was briefly supported with pressors in the ICU. Workup ruled out pulmonary embolism, cardiac ischemia, and infection. An echocardiogram revealed an atrial septal defect and mild mitral regurgitation, but preserved heart function. Elevated LDH and new thrombocytopenia prompted evaluation for lymphoma, but imaging showed only a borderline enlarged spleen, and labs indicated polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia, consistent with chronic immune activation from HIV. Her symptoms resolved with supportive care and return to her regular dialysis schedule. Medications were adjusted, including increasing sevelamer for phosphate control and modifying HIV prophylaxis. She was discharged home with follow-up planned in nephrology and infectious disease.
problems: Herpes zoster with other nervous system complications
Kidney dialysis as the cause of abnormal reaction of patient, or of later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of procedure
